english.question: Which of the following words can fit in the blank labelled (A)?
english.common_data:
In the following passage, certain words have been omitted and replaced by blanks. Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

Honesty is one of the most _(A)_ values a person can hold. When we are honest with others, we build trust and strengthen our relationships over time. A person who is known for telling the truth is always _(B)_ by those around them, whether at home, at school, or at work. Being honest does not always mean saying everything that is on your mind - it means not saying things that are untrue or meant to _(C)_ others. Sometimes, being honest takes great courage. It is not easy to admit a mistake or to say something others may not want to hear. However, a moment of honesty, even when it is difficult, can _(D)_ a relationship far more than a comfortable lie ever could. People who choose honesty in their daily lives earn a reputation that is hard to _(E)_ over time, making them trustworthy in both their personal and professional dealings.
english.explanation:
Answer: A

Decorative: Decorative is an adjective meaning used for decoration. It can modify a noun but makes no logical sense when applied to an abstract value like honesty - values are not decorative objects.

Misunderstood: Misunderstood means incorrectly interpreted. Describing honesty as a misunderstood value would imply people fail to grasp it properly - but the passage presents honesty as something universally valued and admired, not a concept people get wrong.

Outdated: Outdated means no longer relevant or modern. The passage argues honesty is timeless and important - calling it outdated directly contradicts the message of the entire passage.

Complicated: While complicated is grammatically usable as an adjective here, it implies honesty is a difficult, tangled value - the exact opposite of the straightforward, positive framing the passage establishes from the very first sentence.

Cherished: Cherished means held as very dear and important. It is warm in tone, precisely positive in meaning, and fits the simple. "One of the most cherished values" is a natural, widely used expression in English for describing something deeply important to people.

The word that can fit is "cherished." Complete sentence: "Honesty is one of the most cherished values a person can hold."

Strengthen: Strengthen means to make more solid or robust. It fits both the comparative structure of the sentence and the positive, encouraging tone of the passage.

The word that can fit is "strengthen." Complete sentence: "a moment of honesty, even when it is difficult, can strengthen a relationship far more than a comfortable lie ever could."

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:

Every year on August 12, the world pauses to mark International Youth Day, and this year’s UN theme, "Different Contexts, Common Aspirations," could not be more apt. From the Swedish schoolgirl's solitary protest to the dusty protest grounds of Jantar Mantar, young people keep proving that age is no barrier to conscience, and conscience, once lit, becomes a torch that others follow. Consider Malala Yousafzai. Shot by the Taliban at fifteen for daring to demand an education, she turned near-death into a global campaign, becoming, at seventeen, the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate in history.

More than a decade on, she still travels the world to education forums, insisting that a girl's right to a classroom is non-negotiable, whatever her country or circumstance. Then you have another torchbearer, Greta Thunberg, who at fifteen sat alone outside the Swedish parliament with a hand-painted sign, and within a year had inspired millions of students worldwide to walk out of classrooms under the banner of Fridays for Future, forcing climate change onto the agenda of governments that had long treated it as tomorrow's problem.
